info.name: Expense Tracker - BVA API Test Collection
info.description: Import-ready BVA API collection for Expense Tracker. Run the whole collection top to bottom via Postman Collection Runner (Setup folder must run first — it establishes a real session, wallet, and category ids that every other folder depends on). The CSV folder is slow by design (see its own description). Cross-checked against docs/api.md and docs/srs.md on 2026-08-18.

item.name: Setup

request.name: Setup - Register test user
request.description: Tolerates EMAIL_TAKEN on re-run — the Login request right after is what actually guarantees a session.

exec: pm.test("Registered, or already exists from a previous run", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 499); });

request.name: Setup - Login test user
request.description: Always runs after Register so every other request in this collection has a valid session cookie, whether Register just created the account or it already existed.

request.name: Setup - Create wallet
request.description: Real wallet, real id captured into {{walletId}} — replaces the old hardcoded placeholder UUID.

request.name: Setup - Get expense category
request.description: Reuses a real default expense category created at registration (BR-14) instead of a hardcoded placeholder UUID.

exec: pm.test("Default expense categories exist", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 299); const items = pm.response.json().items; pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0); pm.collectionVariables.set("categoryId", items[0].id); });

pm.test("Default income categories exist", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 299); const items = pm.response.json().items; pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0); pm.collectionVariables.set("incomeCategoryId", items[0].id); });

item.name: Setup - Create first budget (precondition for BVA-WCB-004)

request.name: Setup - Create first budget (precondition for BVA-WCB-004)
request.description: BVA-WCB-004 tests that a SECOND budget for the same category+month is rejected — this request guarantees the first one exists. Accepts BUDGET_EXISTS (4xx) on re-run as success too, since the precondition is still satisfied.

exec: pm.test("Precondition budget exists (created now or already existed)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 499); });

item.description: Runs once at the start of every Collection Runner pass. Establishes a real session, a real wallet, and real category ids so every BVA test below exercises the actual boundary rule instead of failing on a stale placeholder id.

item.name: Setup - Generate 5 prior failed login attempts (precondition for rate-limit boundary)

request.name: Setup - Generate 5 prior failed login attempts (precondition for rate-limit boundary)
request.description: Self-looping: LOGIN_ATTEMPT_LIMIT is 6 and checked as recentFailures >= 6 BEFORE credentials are verified, so BVA-AUTH-007 (the true 6th attempt) and BVA-AUTH-008 (the true 7th) only make sense if 5 failures already exist. Uses {{rateLimitEmail}} (a fresh throwaway address, set once in the prerequest script) instead of {{testEmail}} so this doesn't also rate-limit the Setup account's own login for the next 15 minutes.

exec: pm.test("Failed attempt recorded (still under the limit)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.equal(401); });
pm.execution.setNextRequest('Setup - Generate 5 prior failed login attempts (precondition for rate-limit boundary)');
pm.test("Expected status: Requests remain within allowed failure threshold", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.equal(401); });

item.name: Setup - Re-login test user (restore session after Authentication tests)

request.name: Setup - Re-login test user (restore session after Authentication tests)
request.description: BVA-AUTH-002..006 each register a new throwaway user, which auto-logs-in and silently replaces the active session cookie. Every folder after this one assumes the ORIGINAL Setup user's session — this restores it.

exec: pm.test("Session restored to the Setup test user", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200, 299); });

item.name: BVA - CSV

request.name: Setup - Bulk generate export transactions
request.description: Self-looping request (via pm.execution.setNextRequest): posts one transaction, then re-runs itself until {{exportSeedTarget}} transactions exist for this run's wallet. Default target is 10000 to match EXPORT_MAX_ROWS in docs/api.md — this makes the CSV folder slow (thousands of real HTTP round-trips). Lower {{exportSeedTarget}} for a quick smoke run; only the true 10000/10001 boundary actually proves the cap.

exec: pm.test("Not truncated at exactly 10000 rows", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has("X-Export-Truncated")).to.equal(false); });

item.name: Setup - Add 1 more export transaction (now target+1 total)

request.name: Setup - Add 1 more export transaction (now target+1 total)
request.description: Pushes the count to exportSeedTarget+1 so BVA-RCF-009 (the 'above max' case) has a genuinely different dataset from BVA-RCF-008.

item.description: Expensive folder: seeds thousands of transactions via a self-looping request before it can validate the EXPORT_MAX_ROWS boundary for real. Consider running this folder separately from the rest.
